1#א: Something that has a permitted aspect. See what Peleti wrote — why did it enter his mind to be lenient in a doubt of chadash on 16 Nisan — see there.
1#ב: Even if there is doubt, etc. This is regarding an egg laid on Yom Tov after Shabbat, where there is a Torah prohibition — then a double doubt does not help, for there is doubt in the item itself and sixty in the mixture; but regarding an egg laid on ordinary Yom Tov, which is only a rabbinic decree of Yom Tov after Shabbat — we are not stringent in a double doubt; so is the opinion of Magen Avraham; and see what Peleti wrote in resolving the Gemara.
1#ג: Not in its kind — regarding something that has a permitted aspect all agree specifically in its kind; and the reason — see what Peleti wrote in the name of Ran.
1#ד: Nullified in sixty — and everyone follows the name, since it is forbidden in any amount without sixty.
1#ה: If one whitened it — and Peri Chadash disagrees, that appearance in a rabbinic matter has no substance; and see what Peleti wrote — his words are not correct, for everyone agrees that since it came for appearance it is as its kind.
2#א: There are those who say — they wrote in the language "there are those who say," even though we do not find explicitly in poskim who disagree; nevertheless, since Or Zarua gave the reason that therefore it is not a doubt called something that has a permitted aspect when Eliyahu comes, because the food spoils — we learn he does not hold this reasoning "who knows that Eliyahu will permit"; and what Shach and Peri Chadash wrote that so is implied from the Gemara — see what Peleti wrote — nothing is implied.
2#ב: Therefore egg, etc. — and it is not a double doubt, for there is one doubt in the item and one in the mixture — it is not a double doubt.
2#ג: Because the permitting matter — and what Tzemach Tzedek challenged in contradiction: if it will be permitted also now it is permitted, and if forbidden nevertheless permitted because nullified — see Peleti.
3#א: Because one must, etc. — and Maharil disagrees, that in minor outlay it is called something that has a permitted aspect; and he gave a great principle: if the outlay is equal to the prohibition, even if the whole mixture is worth more, it is called great outlay; but in less it is called minor outlay and is within something that has a permitted aspect; and see Peleti — one should be concerned for Maharil.
3#ב: To kasher it and to whiten it — it is possible the vessel cracked through whitening in fire and it is as food that spoils.
3#ג: And all similar cases — and Shach's opinion is to wait until twelve months, then it returns to its permission from the Torah; and even so, d'rabbanan it is forbidden — see Peleti.
4#א: Where the food spoils — and if it is not as esteemed as now we have no concern, since it is not spoiled; for an egg laid on Yom Tov is something that has a permitted aspect since one can wait until tomorrow — and the matter is known that a day-old egg is more esteemed.
4#ב: But its taste is nullified — this is when there is no substance at all, such as placing an egg in the dish and removing it whole and only taste remains in the pot — this is permitted; but if the egg dissolved it is forbidden — see Peleti.
4#ג: If its prohibition is not on account of itself — meaning: absorption itself cannot forbid, for it is kind in not its kind; only it is prohibition of benefit and it is in its kind. It teaches not like the opinion of R' Yehudah that the piece itself is called by the name of the absorbing prohibition that forbids it and is kind in not its kind.
4#ד: Since it is permitted for roasting — and even though we say explicitly in chapter Orlah regarding terumah: even though one can give it to a kohen, nevertheless it is not something that has a permitted aspect, because the kohen was never forbidden; likewise here for roasting it was never forbidden — there for two people: for the kohen it was not forbidden and for the Israelite it was never permitted; unlike here for one person forbidden in cooking and permitted in roasting — one can well say it is something that has a permitted aspect, for we tell him "until you eat it in prohibition eat it in permission" — investigate.
4#ה: That was not recognizable — such as a vat full of grapes in clusters and much wine already dripped from it before Shabbat, and on Shabbat too wine drips from them and it is little and nullified; only one might say it is something that has a permitted aspect — it teaches not, since the dripping wine on Shabbat was never recognizable — and see Peleti who says one can say otherwise first-first it is nullified.
4#ו: For it is possible — and terumah is different, for there is no mitzvah to ask; but vows — there is a mitzvah to ask, for everyone who vows is as if he built a high place.
4#ז: Becomes forbidden again — meaning that same thing, not that the prohibition returns like chadash where the body of the thing does not return, only the prohibition — and see Peleti at the beginning of this siman.
4#ח: And there are those who disagree — even though we forbid chametz even mere taste, for in chametz they were stringent as in not its kind.
4#ט: One who cooks on Shabbat — intentionally, forbidden to him forever and permitted to others — as written; since it is not permitted to him it is not called something that has a permitted aspect — see Peleti.
